references.title: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
references.summary: Spaceflight stressors can change the cardiovascular system. The prototype displays a simulated resting heart-rate trend as one illustrative measurement.
references.limitation: Heart-rate trends alone cannot identify cardiovascular disease or the need for treatment.

references.title: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
references.summary: Sleep loss and irregular schedules are studied as human-spaceflight performance risks. ARES displays fictional sleep duration over time.
references.limitation: Sleep duration alone does not measure sleep quality, circadian alignment or mental health.

references.title: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
references.summary: NASA studies exercise and fitness in microgravity. ARES displays illustrative daily activity minutes to help users inspect a trend.
references.limitation: Activity minutes alone cannot establish fitness, prescribed exercise adherence or injury risk.

references.title: Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight
references.summary: NASA describes radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and hostile or closed environments as major spaceflight hazards.
references.limitation: ARES does not measure these hazards or estimate exposure-related health risks.

references.title: Monitoring Radiation for Astronaut Health
references.summary: The Canadian Space Agency describes technology for monitoring astronaut radiation exposure.
references.limitation: ARES has no radiation sensor, dosimeter, or radiation-exposure input. This is background only.

evidence.usage: Background research links only, not imported NASA/CSA health data.
